title: Write test stand-in scripts from a child process to avoid ETXTBSY
summary: Add one shared test helper that writes an executable stand-in script via a short-lived `sh -c 'cat > tmp && chmod 755 tmp && mv tmp final'` child fed on stdin, so the test process never holds a write handle. Switch all six listed test sites to it, add a fork-stress test, and record the decision, shard-timing and CHANGELOG entries. Audience: developers and CI running the Linux test suite.

defaults_applied.how: stress test added; cargo test and clippy must pass
verifier runs cargo test and checks the recorded ETXTBSY count
criteria check real write-then-exec under forking, not file existence
fixes the cause (held write handle) instead of retrying
uses std::process and sh rather than a new crate dependency for the write itself
the outcome is no ETXTBSY under fork stress
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs (tests around lines 495-552, set_permissions at 438-478), crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs (testutil module at 1093), crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs (retry helper at ~45, stand-in at ~618-645), crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs (~998-1009), crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs (~8141-8156, already matches 'Text file busy'), crates/athena-core/src/test_support.rs, xtask/src/main.rs (stand_in_claude ~833), crates/athena-cli/tests/reconcile.rs (~140). No record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are not touched. Entry point is the helper called by each test; the property is measured directly by exercising real write-then-exec cycles, not through a stand-in.

No existing helper is shared across xtask, athena-cli tests, athena-agent, athena-core and athena-git, so the shared helper needs a home every one of them can dev-depend on; I assume a small new dev-only workspace crate (or an existing one if the dependency graph allows), which means Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock change.

The stress test lives in the helper's home (a new test file or module), forks from other threads (e.g. spawning `true`) while the main thread loops write-then-exec; the in-process variant (std::fs::write then exec) is reported with its measured ETXTBSY count on this machine, printed in test output.

Existing ETXTBSY retry code in claude.rs and reading.rs may be removed or left; I leave production code untouched and only change test code, apart from removing now-redundant test-only retries if they sit in test modules.
The decision covering crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs is D08 (docs/decision-links.toml line ~180); the appended entry says it was checked and stands, with its link.
Non-Linux/non-unix cfg gating is kept as existing tests are unix-only.

acceptance_criteria.text: Grep for `set_permissions` and `from_mode(0o755)` in xtask/src/main.rs, crates/athena-cli/tests/reconcile.rs, crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs, crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs, crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs and crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs shows no test code writing an executable stand-in itself; each such test calls the one shared helper.

The helper's source starts a child process (sh) with the script bytes on stdin that runs cat to a temp file, chmod 755, then mv to the final path, and waits for it; it never opens the script for writing in the test process.

Run `cargo test` for the stress test: many write-then-exec cycles with other threads forking pass with the helper with zero ETXTBSY, and an in-process-write variant prints/records its ETXTBSY count on this machine in the test output (at least once, or the test documents how often it hit).
`cargo test --locked` passes across the workspace, `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.

docs/decisions.md has an appended entry for the decision covering crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs saying it was checked and stands, and docs/decision-links.toml carries its link; the repo's decision-link check passes under cargo test.
xtask/shard-timings.txt lists any new test file or unit added by the change (and Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock list any new crate).
CHANGELOG.md has an entry that describes only what the diff does, no more.
No secrets, credentials or personal data are committed; the helper and test are documented for an outside reader.

out_of_scope: Retries at run sites or in production code
Changing production behavior of claude.rs or other non-test code
departures: Touches six crates plus a possible new shared crate, docs and a stress test, so slightly costlier and riskier than the reference.
urgent_reason: Removes flaky ETXTBSY test failures that cause failed CI attempts and rerun waste.
